story: On July 4, 1997, NASA's Mars Pathfinder mission made history by landing the first wheeled vehicle on another planet. Enclosed in a giant protective cushion of airbags, the spacecraft bounced onto the rocky plain of Ares Vallis before opening its petals to release Sojourner. Named after civil rights crusader Sojourner Truth, the tiny 23-pound microrover was designed for a primary mission of just seven to eight days. Instead, it operated on Mars for 85 Earth days, transmitting 550 images and analyzing rocks like Barnacle Bill using its onboard Alpha Proton X-Ray Spectrometer. The lander, designated the Carl Sagan Memorial Station, lost contact on September 27, 1997. Sojourner's findings provided compelling early evidence that ancient Mars was once warm and wet. Today, a twin rover named Marie Curie resides at the Smithsonian, while NASA's Perseverance rover carries Sojourner's iconic silhouette on its deck.
angle: NASA's first Martian rover was a 23-pound microrover that bounced onto Mars wrapped in giant airbags and outlasted its planned lifespan by months.

claims.claim: Sojourner landed on Mars on July 4, 1997, as part of NASA's Mars Pathfinder mission.
Sojourner was a six-wheeled robotic rover weighing 10.6 kilograms (23 pounds).
Pathfinder used an innovative landing system involving airbags to cushion its impact on the surface of Mars.
Sojourner was named in honor of abolitionist and civil rights activist Sojourner Truth.
The Pathfinder lander was officially named the Carl Sagan Memorial Station after the astronomer's death.
The landing site was located in Ares Vallis, an ancient Martian flood plain.
Ares Vallis was chosen because its rocks were believed to have been deposited by a catastrophic ancient flood.
Sojourner carried an Alpha Proton X-Ray Spectrometer (APXS) to analyze the chemical composition of Martian rocks and soil.
Sojourner was equipped with three onboard cameras.
Sojourner transmitted 550 images back to Earth during its mission.
Data collected by Pathfinder and Sojourner suggested that ancient Mars was once warm and wet.
The final communication session with the mission took place on September 27, 1997, after 85 Earth days of operation.
A fully operational duplicate flight spare named Marie Curie was built and later transferred to the Smithsonian National Air and Space Museum.
NASA's Perseverance rover carries an external plate featuring a visual lineup of Mars rovers starting with Sojourner.

disputed: Sojourner's active sol count varies between sources: S1 states 83 sols (85 Earth days), while S7 states 70 Martian sols (85 Earth days). The script should emphasize 85 Earth days.

Camera color details differ: S1 and S4 describe two front monochrome cameras and one rear color camera, whereas S7 states two color cameras and one black-and-white camera. A script should simply refer to three onboard cameras.
